title: Support Conductor: Playbook Templating and Safe Execution
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Oncall engineers regularly run ad-hoc scripts and multi-step runbooks during incidents. Current runbook artifacts are inconsistent (markdown, spreadsheets, Playbooks-as-docs) and lack typed inputs, guardrails, or dry-run support. This increases repair time and surface for human error.

Goal: Deliver a 'Support Conductor' subsystem that provides: (1) a declarative playbook templating DSL for ops steps, (2) safe execution harness with stageable dry-run and permission checks, (3) integrated telemetry and outcome provenance for post-incident review, and (4) first-class GitHub + Console integration for authoring and canary rollouts.

Scope: Build templating + execution runtime for common admin utilities (db toggles, cache flushes, scaled restarts) and a UI surface in Console for editors and run-once execution. This work focuses on core runtime, RBAC checks, audit events, and a CI/PR validation step for playbooks. Console UX and advanced scheduling are out of scope for this ticket and will be follow-ups.

Proposed design summary:
- Templating language: YAML-based schema with typed inputs, parameter validation, and conditional steps. Reuse existing step primitives from opslet library where possible.
- Execution harness: sandboxed runner with idempotency keys, dry-run mode (simulated calls and no side-effect gating), and step-level safety checks.
- Permissions: integrate with RBAC service; require elevated session for high-risk steps (e.g., DB write, scale down).
- Telemetry: emit structured outcome events to Console tracing and add explicit links to incident timelines.
- CI validation: GitHub Actions that run static checks (schema, forbidden ops, TTL) and a linter that flags unsafe patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Author can commit a templated playbook and pass CI static checks (schema + linter).
2) Oncall can execute playbook in dry-run mode via CLI/Console and see deterministic simulated outputs.
3) Safe execution blocks high-risk steps without an elevated session; blocked steps are logged and surfaced in the UI and audit logs.
4) Every run emits a provenance event with step outcomes, invocation metadata, and idempotency token.
5) Integration tests for three sample playbooks (cache flush, rolling restart, feature toggle) exist and run in CI.

Rollout plan: internal beta for SREs then broader rollout to Support. Monitor errors, time-to-complete, and any accidental production side-effects for two weeks before promoting to Default Runner for all teams.

Notes: this ticket should coordinate with ENG-314159 (scheduler) for any future automation and ENG-517200 for telemetry schema alignment.

2026-03-05 - Design Review (Louisa Park): Reviewed Console surface mockups. UX asks: show 'dry-run' clearly with simulated diff and emphasize which steps will be gated. Created Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/ConductorMockups
